correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(m\ge2,\ t\ge1\) the Hilbert barycenter identity gives \(C^2\ge 2(m-1)/m+1\); orthogonal regular-simplex+antipodal-pair embedding meets the sharp distortion. Equality in the same identity for every pair class yields common centers, regular simplex, antipodal unit directions perpendicular to its span, and all cross distances fixed. Comparing all four distances between any two pair classes yields the iff coherence cutoff \(\mu_m=(m-2)/(2m)\); orthogonal span additivity proves exact minimum affine dimension. At m=2 the cutoff is 0 and rank=t. At \(m\ge3\) volume packing and random-sign union bound give the log dimension growth. The Welch trace-rank inequality proves the finite (m,t)=(3,7) rank 6. Exact-rational checks are supplied but not used for universal inference.

value.rationale: The answer is a structural equivalence between the full family of distortion-optimal embeddings of a natural graph metric and spherical line codes, not a redundant evaluation of the bipartite scalar. The sharp phase transition from optimal affine dimension t+1 at m=2 to \(m-1+\Theta_m(\log(t+1))\) for each fixed \(m\ge3\), at distortion independent of t, is a motivated and meaningful phenomenon, with explicit quantitative bounds and an exact finite code-rank example.
